text:
incident-bot: pager triggered -> P1 reserved-capacity latency spike for tenant starlight-health :rotating_light:

pagerduty: P1 | ReservedPoolLatency | tenant=starlight-health | threshold=95p latency 1.2s (SLO 300ms) | auto-escalate=true

maria (oncall): acked via PD, jumping in. seeing a burst in 95p on the reserved pool graphs. anyone oncall for dedicated pools?

kevin (sre): i can hop in. looks like KV cache eviction count spiked, followed by many cold KV misses. tail latency bump across the tenant's reserved pool.

maria (oncall): is the reserved pool saturated or are requests queuing? metrics -> https://dash.redwood.internal/tenants/starlight-health/reserved-pool

sam (infra): autoscaler didn't kick because headroom metric stayed > configured threshold, but we got a lot of short lived connections from their nightly batch. reserved allocations are pinned.

maria (oncall): summary for pager: tenant starlight-health, reserved pool showing 95p > 1s, 5xx rate ~0.6% recent spike, customer-facing latency increased. PD page fired.

kevin (sre): running quick checks. tail logs show repeated `KVCache::evict()` churn + OOM-ish GC spikes on nodes:

```
# sample from node-12
[2026-03-15T03:12:01Z] KVCache: evict key=usr-83f... size=3.1MB
[2026-03-15T03:12:02Z] Runtime: mem pressure high, reclaiming caches
[2026-03-15T03:12:02Z] http: 503 serving request id=abc123 tenant=starlight-health
```

kevin (sre): hypothesis: their batch caused a KV cache storm, causing local memory pressure and blocking inference workers -> higher queue latency and occasional 503s.

maria (oncall): mitigation options? can we expand reserved pool temporarily or scale to shared fallback?

sam (infra): we can do either: 1) bump reserved pool capacity by +2 instances (fast) 2) enable tenant fallback to shared pool (risk: cost + mixed-tenancy perf) 3) restart affected nodes to flush cache (risky, will disrupt in-flight requests).

kevin (sre): prefer (1) + quick cache heuristics. I'll propose: bump reserved pool by 2, enable prefix KV cache TTL shortening for tenant to reduce eviction churn, and watch for improvement.

maria (oncall): do it. sam, can you run the scale now? include change in PD notes and link to runbook.

sam (infra): scaling now. running command:

```
redwoodctl reserved-pools scale --tenant starlight-health --add 2 --reason "oncall emergency: KV eviction spike"
```

sam (infra): command accepted, provisioning 2 nodes. ETA ~ 90s. ops-runbook-bot: posting checklist.

ops-runbook-bot: Checklist posted -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/dedicated/kv-eviction

kevin (sre): while nodes come up, i'll push a temporary KV TTL override for the tenant to 30s (was 5m) to reduce large cache items persisting. running config patch:

```
redwoodctl kv-config set --tenant starlight-health --max-item-ttl 30s --mode temp
```

maria (oncall): noted. also switching routing policy to prefer warm nodes for this tenant to reduce cold misses.

sam (infra): new nodes are up and healthy, reserved pool capacity increased. graphs showing 95p dropping from 1.2s -> 420ms within 60s. 5xx rate trending down.

kevin (sre): latency improving but still above SLO. KV eviction rate trending down after TTL override. we'll leave fallback disabled for now.

maria (oncall): customer impact update: starlight-health reported intermittent elevated latency for 12 minutes, about 2% of requests saw 5xx/timeout. we've mitigated with +2 nodes and TTL override.

pagerduty: escalation cleared by maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): i'm going to hand off for postmortem and follow-up with infra/runcfg tomorrow. kevin, can you take the follow-up and own the postmortem? include root cause hypothesis and recommend config changes (autoscaler thresholds, tenant KV defaults).

kevin (sre): taking it. i'll collect logs, allocate postmortem doc, and propose a conservative autoscaler tweak + a safeguard to auto-fallback to shared pool if reserved pool CPU or KV eviction rate crosses thresholds for >2m.

maria (oncall): thanks. leaving notes:
- action taken: scaled reserved pool +2 nodes; TTL override to 30s; routing preference to warm nodes.
- immediate impact: P95 down to ~420ms, 5xx down to baseline.
- follow-up: kevin to own postmortem and config PR.

kevin (sre): i'll start doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/3972001234-starlight-kv-eviction

maria (oncall): handing off now. if it flares again, page the oncall rotation. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

kevin (sre): noted, will post final mitigations and timeline after analysis.

incident-bot: thread closed by maria (oncall) after escalation cleared.
